provenance.instrument: Lower Windsor Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 470 Zoning, Ord. No. 2003-02 of 4-10-2003, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 LO4166, Township of Lower Windsor. 470-7B names the 'Lower Windsor Township, York County, Pennsylvania Zoning Map', so this is Lower Windsor township, York County. The use table (Table 470-8) and the density and dimensional table (Table 470-12) are text in Article III, and the attachments are figures and the map. Floodplain management is Chapter 235 (named in 470-18B(3)). New Laws: none
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 shows the version date 2026-02-12 beside the Code link. New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.' Chapter 470 history: as amended through Ord. No. 2012-01 of 4-12-2012, later amendments noted where applicable
checks: Accessory garage apartment or rental cottage: 'An accessory dwelling unit clearly incidental to the single-family detached dwelling located on the same lot' (470-6). Table 470-8 lists it only in the Village District (V), by special exception. 470-8: 'The uses listed as permitted in each district are the only uses permitted in that district'

Its standards: clearly accessory to the single-family detached dwelling, only one per lot, 'One development right is required for each accessory garage apartment or rental cottage', the building coverage of the house, accessory structures and the unit together within the district's maximum lot coverage, and one off-street space 'with unrestricted ingress and egress' beyond the house's parking (470-52). The house needs 2 spaces, so 3 in all (470-36B)

In V the unit is 'permitted on any building site having enough building site area to permit two or more dwelling units', may occupy at most 35% of the required rear yard, may be at most 50% of the total square footage of the principal structure, may not stand in front of the house's front facade or the front setback, and keeps 5 ft side and rear yards. A lawful existing nonconforming garage apartment may remain (470-15H(5)). 470-15H is headed as design recommendations, and 470-8 makes Table 470-8 set the path, so the unit is read as a special exception

Development rights: in V a parcel that existed when the chapter was adopted in 2003 is granted rights at the base density of 2.0 per acre of adjusted tract area, one for each 21,780 sq ft, and more (up to 6.0) only with transferred rights (470-12B, D, 470-15F, Table 470-12). A right is used by each new lot, principal structure or use created after that date (470-6 'Development right'). Whether a lot has a right left for the unit depends on the parcel's history. Ask the zoning officer

Two-family dwellings (2 units on 1 lot) are permitted by right in R, V and WR, at the per-unit lot areas of Table 470-12 (6,000 sq ft in R and 3,000 sq ft in V and WR with public water and sewer, 20,000 or 15,000 with one of them, 37,500 with neither). A two-family residential conversion is by right in R, V and WR and by special exception in AG, and uses one development right per added unit, keeps the character of the existing building and meets parking and minimum habitable floor area (Table 470-8, 470-130). Table 470-12 marks two-family dwellings 'Not Permitted' in AG. A multifamily residential conversion (more than two units) is a special exception in R, V and WR (470-109). A caretaker or watchman dwelling accessory to an agricultural, professional, commercial or industrial use is a special exception in AG, V, WR and I, on a lot of at least 20 acres (470-6, Table 470-8, 470-77)
Accessory buildings may be 25 ft tall in every district (Table 470-12)

Restricted Development Overlay: slopes over 15%, wetlands and the 100-year floodplain. No site disturbance on slopes over 25%, a grading plan for slopes of 15% to 25%, no building in wetlands except under DEP and Army Corps permits, no well or septic system in a wetland, and floodplain land not built upon except in strict compliance with this chapter, Chapter 410 and the other codes (470-18E)

Lot coverage: Table 470-12 'Maximum Lot Coverage' is a share of the lot that 'can be covered with an impervious surface', and buildings and structures count as impervious surface (470-6 'Lot coverage, maximum', 'Impervious surface'). So the district figures (AG 20%, R, V and WR 55%) are impervious cover

Uses not provided for: 'Any use not specifically allowed elsewhere in this chapter shall be allowed by special exception in the district or districts where, and to the extent that, similar uses are permitted' (470-9). The accessory garage apartment is allowed in V, so outside V it is read as not listed there

Accessory structures: 'Apartments or other living quarters, except as specifically provided for elsewhere in this chapter, shall not be permitted in an accessory structure' (470-31B). Only 470-52 provides for them, in V. An accessory structure attached to the house is part of the house for all regulatory purposes (470-31A). A detached one may stand in any yard outside the required front setback, at least 5 ft from the side and rear lines, at most 25 ft tall (470-31B, C)

Minimum habitable floor area: 650 sq ft per unit for single-family and two-family dwellings, 500 sq ft per unit for two-family and multifamily conversions (470-35). The garage apartment is not named there, so its own minimum is not settled. Parking: 2 spaces per unit for a house, a two-family dwelling and a conversion, 1 for the garage apartment and for a caretaker dwelling (470-36B)

Streams and services: no land within 25 ft of the ordinary waterline of a stream on the Zoning Map or of the Susquehanna River may be altered, regraded or filled except as 470-48 allows. Public water and sewer approved by DEP must be used, or proof given that the on-site system can serve the added units (470-49)

Floodplain (Chapter 235, Ord. No. 2015-03): the floodplain is the FIRM of December 16, 2015 or its latest revision and any community-identified flood hazard areas (235-18A). 'Within any identified floodplain area any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited', with relief only by a variance under Article VII, and no variance may raise the base flood elevation (235-24, 235-34A(1)). An accessory structure there 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' (235-24E(1)). New construction is a structure begun on or after December 16, 2015, with its later improvements. The regulatory flood elevation is the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft. No new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank in an AE area without a floodway, unless DEP issues a permit (235-19B(2)(b)). Much of WR is in the 100-year floodplain (470-16A)

Variances and special exceptions: the Zoning Hearing Board decides on the findings of 470-150C, with no bar on a use variance. A special exception meets the general standards of 470-151F, including adequate water, sewage disposal and storm drainage. Either expires if no zoning or building permit is obtained within six months (470-150A(2), 470-151A(2))

Not read: Chapter 335 (Rental Property) and Chapter 355 (Short-Term Rentals). A rental cottage let to a tenant may need a rental license or registration there. The Historic Overlay asks only for voluntary photo documentation before exterior alteration or demolition, so it adds no review (470-19C). Temporary housing for farm workers (a seasonal mobile or manufactured home on a farm of 50 acres) is not an ADU (470-81)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Lower Windsor Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360, one page at a time, on 2026-11-18: the Chapter 470 table of contents, Article III to the start of 470-18E(1)(b) (print view), Table 470-8 rows for dwellings, the accessory garage apartment and conversions (on the page, as the print view loses the columns), 470-6 definitions from A to 'Noncommercial keeping of animals', 470-52 and 470-130. Read on a second check the same day: 470-18 and 470-19 in full, Article V (470-30 to 470-49), Article VI 470-50 to 470-54, 470-75 to 470-81, 470-106 to 470-109 and 470-128 to 470-133, Article VIII (470-148 to 470-151) and Chapter 235 Floodplain Management to 235-34 with its definitions. Not read: Articles I, IV, VII (transferable development rights), IX, 470-20, 470-21, the rest of Article VI, the definitions after 'Noncommercial keeping of animals', Chapters 335 and 355, and the zoning map (PDF).

value.name: Caretaker or watchman dwelling (AG, V, WR, I)
value.conditions: A single-family detached dwelling unit accessory to an agricultural, professional, commercial or industrial use, for the owner or an employee and their immediate family, to care for and protect people, property, animals or equipment on the site, under the same ownership. 'The minimum lot area for the principal use: 20 acres'. One parking space (470-36B)

requires.condition: An agricultural, professional, commercial or industrial principal use on the lot
One development right is available for the dwelling, except in the Industrial District

value.note: 20 acres is 871,200 sq ft, the lot of the principal use (470-77B)

value.condition: One development right is required for the unit. In V a parcel that existed when the chapter was adopted in 2003 holds rights at the base density of 2.0 per acre of adjusted tract area, one for each 21,780 sq ft, and more (up to 6.0) only with transferred rights. A right is used by each new lot, principal structure or use created after that date. So without transferred rights the unit needs about 21,780 sq ft of adjusted tract area if the house came before 2003, and about 43,560 sq ft if the house used a right too. Ask the zoning officer.
The unit is accessory to a single-family detached dwelling.

The building coverage of the house, other accessory structures and the unit together may not exceed the district's maximum lot coverage. That lot coverage counts every impervious surface, paving as well as buildings.

Restricted Development Overlay (slopes over 15%, wetlands, 100-year floodplain): no site disturbance on slopes over 25%, a grading plan for 15% to 25%. No building in wetlands except under DEP and Army Corps permits, and no well or septic system in a wetland. Floodplain land is not built upon except in strict compliance with this chapter and the other codes, and Chapter 235 prohibits new construction there without a variance.

Within any identified floodplain area 'any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited'. Only a variance opens it, on the criteria of Chapter 235 Article VII, heard by the Zoning Hearing Board, and no variance may raise the base flood elevation. With a variance a new dwelling has its lowest floor above the regulatory flood elevation, the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft. Fill and manufactured homes are prohibited there. The floodplain is the FIRM of December 16, 2015 or its latest revision and any community-identified flood hazard areas.

In an identified floodplain area an accessory structure 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may have no sanitary facilities. Raising it as a dwelling is new construction or a substantial improvement, which 235-24 prohibits without a variance.

New construction is a structure begun on or after December 16, 2015, with its later improvements. In an identified floodplain area an addition to such a house, or a unit made inside it, is new construction, which 235-24 prohibits without a variance.

In an identified floodplain area, work on a house begun before December 16, 2015 that costs 50% or more of its market value is a substantial improvement, prohibited without a variance. Smaller work is elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible. No enlargement may raise the base flood elevation.

no_variance.quote: No variance shall be granted within any identified floodplain area that would cause any increase in BFE.
no_variance.note: Reaches only work that would raise the base flood elevation

value.condition: In an AE area without a floodway no new construction or development may be located within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of any watercourse, unless DEP issues a permit.
